what_it_does: Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) are cryptographic puzzles that prove knowledge of a secret without revealing it—useful for blockchain and privacy. Proof generation involves multiple computation stages (like integer multiplication in special fields, polynomial operations), each with different demands. Existing accelerators are rigid: each stage needs its own specialized circuit, wasting resources. LegoZK uses modular building blocks (finite field arithmetic units—circuits for math in special number systems) wired through a flexible network. By reconfiguring these units and the network between proof stages, one accelerator handles all stages efficiently without wasted hardware.
